key_insight: Allowing a small positive training error at finite temperature preserves wide, accessible solution regions and extends the overlap-gap threshold beyond the zero-temperature limit.
engineering_relevance: For neural network optimization, controlled thermal noise can make otherwise hard non-convex regimes more searchable while still supporting good generalization.
method: Analyze the finite-temperature Gibbs measure for binary perceptrons.
Derive a criterion for when smoothing the loss near the decision boundary removes freezing.
Extend the OGP construction to finite energy and test a message-passing solver numerically.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a finite-energy message-passing algorithm that numerically demonstrates effective generalization in the regime where zero-temperature solution recovery is computationally hard.
watch_item: The benefits depend on the loss smoothness and allowed error level, so the approach may not transfer unchanged to models with different boundaries or training objectives.
paper_title: On the robustness of noisy solutions in non-convex neural networks
